content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The tumor is the large, heterogeneous hyperintense mass in the posterior compartment. On the left panel it spans roughly x 200–450 and y 370–670. In the right panel the same region sits at about x 990–1240.

Marks that fall inside this region:
- 1384, 1382, 1297, 1340, 1374, 1337, 1336, 1289, 1334, 1367, 1241.

The centre of the mass is about x 1100–1120 (right panel), y 530–560. Mark 1374, at (1147, 553), is the closest to that point. It is marked as a circle, which may denote a special marker, but it still lies well within the tumor. Mark 1289, at (1113, 605), is also inside the tumor but lower, nearer the center of the bright solid region. Mark 1374 sits near the middle of the whole mass, so I chose it.

ANSWER: 1374
